points.title: 早期教育与科学启蒙
points.description: 皮亚杰出生于瑞士纳沙泰尔的一个知识分子家庭，父亲是中世纪文学教授。从小就表现出对自然科学的浓厚兴趣，10岁时发表关于阿尔卑斯山白麻雀的观察报告。在纳沙泰尔大学学习期间，他对哲学和生物学产生浓厚兴趣，1918年获得自然科学博士学位，发表关于软体动物分类学的论文。这一时期奠定了他跨学科研究的基础，也培养了他对生物适应与认知发展的初步思考。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Neuchâtel, Switzerland to an intellectual family with a father who was a professor of medieval literature, Piaget showed early interest in natural sciences. At age 10, he published his first scientific paper on an albino sparrow. During his studies at the University of Neuchâtel, he developed interests in both philosophy and biology, earning his doctorate in natural sciences in 1918 with a thesis on mollusk taxonomy. This period established his interdisciplinary approach and laid the groundwork for his thinking on biological adaptation and cognitive development.

points.title: 心理实验室经历
points.description: 第一次世界大战后，皮亚杰前往巴黎，在比奈实验室工作，负责标准化智力测试。在测试过程中，他注意到儿童对问题的回答与成人逻辑不同，这引发了他对儿童思维方式的深入研究。他发现儿童不是简单地'错误'回答，而是有着自己独特的逻辑系统。这一发现促使他放弃标准化测试研究，转向对儿童认知发展的自然观察和实验研究，为日后创立认知发展理论奠定基础。
points.descriptionEn: After World War I, Piaget moved to Paris and worked at the Binet Laboratory, where he was responsible for standardizing intelligence tests. During his work, he noticed that children's answers to questions differed from adult logic in systematic ways, sparking his deep interest in children's thinking patterns. He discovered that children weren't simply 'wrong' but had their own logical systems. This insight led him to abandon standardized testing research and转向 naturalistic observation and experimental study of children's cognitive development, laying the foundation for his later theory of cognitive development.

points.title: 教育实践与研究
points.description: 1921年，皮亚杰接受日内瓦卢梭学院的邀请，开始从事儿童思维研究。他设计了精巧的实验方法观察儿童认知发展，如守恒实验、分类实验等。在此期间，他与妻子瓦伦汀娜合作研究儿童的语言和思维发展。1929年，他开始在日内瓦大学任教，同时担任国际教育局局长。这一时期他发表了《儿童的语言与思维》(1923)、《儿童对世界的现实建构》(1926)等重要著作，开始系统阐述认知发展理论的基本框架。
points.descriptionEn: In 1921, Piaget was invited to the Institute Jean-Jacques Rousseau in Geneva to begin his research on children's thinking. He designed ingenious experimental methods to observe cognitive development, such as conservation and classification tasks. During this time, he collaborated with his wife Valentine on studying children's language and thinking development. In 1929, he began teaching at the University of Geneva while serving as Director of the International Bureau of Education. This period saw the publication of key works like 'The Language and Thought of the Child' (1923) and 'The Child's Construction of Reality' (1926), where he began systematically outlining the framework of his cognitive development theory.

points.title: 认知发展理论体系化
points.description: 这一时期是皮亚杰理论发展的黄金阶段。他在日内瓦大学建立了认知发展研究中心，吸引了来自世界各地的学者。1948年，他创立并领导国际发生认识论研究会。他提出了认知发展的四个阶段理论：感知运动阶段(0-2岁)、前运算阶段(2-7岁)、具体运算阶段(7-11岁)和形式运算阶段(11岁以上)。他强调儿童是'小科学家'，通过同化和顺应主动建构知识。这一时期的重要著作包括《儿童心理学》(1929)、《智力心理学》(1950)和《发生认识论导论》(1950)，他的理论开始在国际上产生广泛影响。
points.descriptionEn: This period marked the golden age of Piaget's theoretical development. At the University of Geneva, he established the Center for Genetic Epistemology, attracting scholars from around the world. In 1948, he founded and directed the International Center for Genetic Epistemology. He formulated his four-stage theory of cognitive development: sensorimotor stage (0-2 years), preoperational stage (2-7 years), concrete operational stage (7-11 years), and formal operational stage (11+ years). He emphasized that children are 'little scientists' who actively construct knowledge through assimilation and accommodation. Key works from this period include 'The Psychology of Intelligence' (1950) and 'Introduction to Genetic Epistemology' (1950), as his theory began to exert widespread international influence.

points.title: 理论完善与国际影响
points.description: 晚年皮亚杰继续完善他的理论，并拓展到跨学科领域。1955年，他创立国际发生认识论研究中心，并担任主任直至去世。他开始将认知发展理论应用于教育、逻辑学、数学和科学哲学等领域。1966年，他发表《结构主义》，将认知发展理论与结构主义哲学相结合。1970年代，他的理论在全球范围内产生深远影响，成为教育改革的重要理论基础。尽管晚年健康不佳，他仍坚持研究，直到1980年在日内瓦去世，享年84岁。他的理论至今仍是发展心理学和教育学的重要基石。
points.descriptionEn: In his later years, Piaget continued to refine his theory and extend it to interdisciplinary fields. In 1955, he founded the International Center for Genetic Epistemology, serving as its director until his death. He began applying cognitive development theory to education, logic, mathematics, and philosophy of science. In 1966, he published 'Structuralism,' integrating his cognitive development theory with structuralist philosophy. During the 1970s, his theory exerted profound global influence, becoming an important theoretical foundation for educational reform. Despite declining health in his later years, he continued his research until his death in Geneva in 1980 at age 84. His theory remains a cornerstone of developmental psychology and education today.

supporter.zh: 皮亚杰被誉为20世纪最伟大的发展心理学家之一，他彻底改变了人们对儿童思维的理解。支持者认为他革命性地证明了儿童不是'不成熟'的成人，而是拥有独特逻辑系统的思考者。他的认知发展理论为现代教育提供了科学基础，强调儿童主动建构知识的重要性。皮亚杰的研究方法严谨创新，开创了自然观察与实验相结合的研究范式，对后世心理学研究产生深远影响。他的跨学科视野和对人类认知本质的探索，使他成为认知科学领域的先驱人物。
supporter.en: Piaget is regarded as one of the greatest developmental psychologists of the 20th century, revolutionizing our understanding of children's thinking. Supporters argue he demonstrated that children are not 'immature' adults but thinkers with unique logical systems. His cognitive development theory provided a scientific foundation for modern education, emphasizing the importance of children actively constructing knowledge. Piaget's rigorous and innovative research methods pioneered a naturalistic-experimental approach that profoundly influenced subsequent psychological research. His interdisciplinary vision and exploration of the nature of human cognition established him as a pioneer in cognitive science.

critic.zh: 批评者指出皮亚杰的理论存在多方面局限。首先，他的样本主要来自瑞士中产阶级儿童，研究结果的普适性受到质疑。其次，他低估了儿童能力的早期发展，现代研究表明婴儿认知能力比他想象的更强。第三，他的阶段理论过于刚性，忽视了个体差异和文化因素对认知发展的影响。此外，他的研究方法被批评为过于结构化，可能无法捕捉儿童自然思维的全貌。最后，一些教育工作者认为他的理论过于强调个体建构，忽视了社会互动和文化传递在认知发展中的重要作用。
critic.en: Critics point out several limitations in Piaget's theory. First, his samples were primarily from Swiss middle-class children, raising questions about the universality of his findings. Second, he underestimated early cognitive development, with modern research showing infants possess stronger abilities than he imagined. Third, his stage theory is considered too rigid, neglecting individual differences and cultural influences on cognitive development. Additionally, his research methods have been criticized as overly structured, potentially failing to capture the full picture of children's natural thinking. Finally, some educators argue his theory overemphasizes individual construction while underplaying the role of social interaction and cultural transmission in cognitive development.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，皮亚杰被视为认知发展理论的奠基人，他的影响力超越了心理学领域，延伸至教育学、人工智能和认知科学。他的'儿童作为科学家'的比喻已成为流行文化中的经典表述。尽管他的理论受到修正和挑战，但核心观点——儿童主动建构知识——已成为现代教育理念的基础。皮亚杰的工作标志着从行为主义到认知革命的转变，他关注思维过程而非仅关注可观察行为，这一转向彻底改变了心理学的发展轨迹。他的名字已成为教育改革和儿童发展研究的代名词，象征着对人类认知本质的持续探索。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Piaget is recognized as the founder of cognitive development theory, with influence extending beyond psychology into education, artificial intelligence, and cognitive science. His metaphor of 'the child as scientist' has become a classic in popular culture. Although his theories have been modified and challenged, the core idea that children actively construct knowledge has become fundamental to modern educational philosophy. Piaget's work marked the shift from behaviorism to the cognitive revolution, focusing on mental processes rather than just observable behavior—a transformation that changed the trajectory of psychology. His name has become synonymous with educational reform and child development research, symbolizing the ongoing exploration of the nature of human cognition.

self.zh: 每一次儿童讲话，每一次儿童的行为，都是一种实验。
self.en: Every time a child speaks, every time a child acts, it is an experiment.

others.zh: 皮亚杰的工作是发展心理学史上最伟大的成就之一，它彻底改变了我们对儿童如何思考的理解。
others.en: Piaget's work is one of the greatest achievements in the history of developmental psychology; it completely changed our understanding of how children think.
